# PR Influencer

> PR Influencer is the influencer PR service brand of influUGC, a creative marketing and media production agency (est. 2020) based in Agouza, Giza, Egypt. It runs influencer public relations for brands in Egypt, Saudi Arabia and the wider Gulf: PR campaigns, creator relations, product seeding, event invitations and brand trips — building credible presence for brands inside creators' content instead of direct paid posts.

## Services (Influencer PR)

- Influencer PR Campaigns: full PR campaigns around product launches, openings and seasonal moments — creator selection, story angles, coordination and coverage reporting.
- Creator Relations: long-term relationships between a brand and a circle of creators who fit its category, with first access to launches and experiences.
- Product Seeding: sending products to carefully selected creators as a designed gifting experience, with delivery and sharing follow-up.
- Event Invitations: targeted guest lists for openings, launches and brand events, with RSVP follow-up and on-site coverage coordination.
- Brand Trips: travel and visit experiences designed for creators around a brand or destination, from programme to guest selection and content coordination.

## Guides (free, on the landing pages)

Published on the homepages (Arabic: https://prinfluencer.net/#guides · English: https://prinfluencer.net/en.html#guides) — practical know-how from how influencer PR programmes are actually run:

- How to invite influencers to an event properly (https://prinfluencer.net/en.html#guide-events): fit before followers, check past event coverage, invite with a specific reason; send one complete invitation early (what/where/when, what is in it for the guest, parking, dress code, plus-one, a named day contact); run the day for coverage — one designed filmable moment, the product in guests' hands, no posting ultimatums; follow up the next day with thanks and the official photos.
- Product seeding that actually gets posted (https://prinfluencer.net/en.html#guide-seeding): seeding works as a designed first experience, not as shipping. Pick fewer, better-matched creators (category fit, existing organic product content, a deliberate size mix); design the unboxing (good packaging, product visible immediately, one short personal note, one clear card); time it to a launch, season or restock; never attach posting strings — follow up once, warmly, and track who posted.
- How to brief an influencer for a launch (https://prinfluencer.net/en.html#guide-brief): the brief makes every post different in voice and identical in facts — product name spelled exactly, launch date, where it sells, the one-line story, two or three backable proof points; leave hook, format and setting to the creator; one practical page covering timing/embargo, deliverables and written usage scope, must-avoids, and a single named contact; never send the brief the night before launch.
